# Base Image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS for a stable, recent environment
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package installations
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies, MPI, FFTW, certificates, and other required libraries
# - build-essential: Compiler toolchain (gcc, g++, make)
# - gfortran: Fortran compiler, required by some LAMMPS packages
# - cmake: Build system generator for LAMMPS
# - git: For cloning the source code from the repository
# - openmpi-bin, libopenmpi-dev: OpenMPI for parallel execution
# - libfftw3-dev: FFTW3 library for KSPACE package
# - ca-certificates: For secure network communications (e.g., git clone)
# - libgomp1: GNU OpenMP library runtime
# - python3, python3-dev: [FIX] Added as a required dependency for the LAMMPS build system
# Clean up apt cache to reduce image size
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y \
    build-essential \
    gfortran \
    cmake \
    git \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    libfftw3-dev \
    ca-certificates \
    libgomp1 \
    python3 \
    python3-dev \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Set a working directory for the build process
WORKDIR /opt

# Clone the latest stable version of LAMMPS, build it, and clean up
# This is done in a single RUN command to reduce image layers and size
RUN git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/lammps/lammps.git && \
    cd lammps && \
    mkdir build && \
    cd build && \
    # Configure the build with CMake
    # - PKG_REAXFF=yes: Enables the ReaxFF package as requested
    # - BUILD_MPI=yes: Enables MPI for parallel execution in containerized environments
    # - PKG_KSPACE=yes: A common package that uses FFTW, good for general use
    # - BUILD_OMP=yes: Enable OpenMP support
    cmake ../cmake \
        -D PKG_REAXFF=yes \
        -D BUILD_MPI=yes \
        -D PKG_KSPACE=yes \
        -D BUILD_OMP=yes && \
    # Build LAMMPS using all available processor cores
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    # Copy the main LAMMPS executable to a directory on the system's PATH
    cp lmp /usr/local/bin/lmp && \
    # Go back to the root of the cloned repo to copy examples
    cd /opt/lammps && \
    # Create the final application directory and copy example files into it
    mkdir -p /app && \
    cp examples/reaxff/HNS/* /app/ && \
    # Clean up the source code to minimize final image size
    cd / && \
    rm -rf /opt/lammps

# Set the final working directory for the container
WORKDIR /app

# Set a default command to provide a shell, allowing users to run commands interactively
# or override with their own mpirun command.
CMD ["/bin/bash"]

# This MiniCluster manifest is designed for a single-node LAMMPS experiment
# on an AWS CPU instance within a Kubernetes cluster using the Flux Operator.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # Name of the MiniCluster instance for the LAMMPS experiment.
  name: lammps-reaxff-hns
  # Deployment will be in the 'default' namespace as requested.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The number of pods in the MiniCluster, set to 1 for a single-node run.
  size: 1

  # The total number of MPI tasks to run across the MiniCluster.
  # Since size is 1, all tasks will run within that single pod.
  tasks: 4

  # When set to false, the job pods and services are not deleted upon completion.
  # This is useful for debugging and inspecting logs and results.
  cleanup: false

  # Flux Operator logging settings.
  logging:
    # Strict mode ensures that any logging-related errors will cause the job to fail.
    strict: true

  # Defines the application container to be managed by Flux.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax
      # The command to be executed by Flux. The Flux Operator will prepend `flux run -n <tasks>`.
      command: lmp -v x 2 -v y 2 -v z 2 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite

      # Set to false as this is the main application container, not a dedicated launcher pod.
      launcher: false

      # Set the working directory to where the LAMMPS input file is located within the container.
      workingDir: /lammps/examples/reaxff/HNS

      # Resource requests and limits are intentionally omitted to allow the pod
      # to be "Burstable" and use available node resources.
      resources: {}
